title: Predictive Cycle Credits: Tiered Surge Allocation and Scoped‑Lite Strategy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: As usage patterns and hires become more variable, teams need a predictable, fair mechanism to request and consume mid‑cycle capacity without stalling launches. This ticket defines a tiered surge credit system plus a minimal 'Scoped‑Lite' plan that product teams can elect when facing partial staffing or unexpected blockers. Goal: produce a playbook, decision matrix, and simulator to be adopted by PMs/EMs that reduces ad‑hoc reassignments and speeds mid‑cycle tradeoffs by 30%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook doc with clear triggers, credit buckets, and approval flow published in Confluence; 2) Lightweight simulator (spreadsheet or internal tool) that models credits vs. risk and shows examples for 3 realistic teams; 3) Pilot run with 2 product teams during 2026-W12; 4) Metrics dashboard tracking credit consumption, scope delta, and launch slippage

decisions: Use three tiers of surge credits (Tier A = 1 FTE-week equivalent, Tier B = 3 FTE-week equivalent, Tier C = 6+ FTE-week emergency bucket).
Scoped‑Lite: mandatory deliverable template with explicit success criteria, automated rollback trigger, and a reduced QA checklist to allow pragmatic launches under capacity constraints.

Approval SLA: Tier A auto-approve for PM+EM sync within 24 hours; Tier B requires VP product or delegated council signoff within 48 hours; Tier C escalates to Platform leadership and Finance for budget impact.
Credits charged against initiative budgets first; unspent credits expire at cycle end and cannot be carried forward without exec approval.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams may over-request credits and mask prioritization issues. Mitigation: hard limit of 2 Tier A requests per team per cycle without retrospective justification.
Risk: Operational load if many teams launch Scoped‑Lite features. Mitigation: require a runbook snippet and emergency rollback path; schedule Scoped‑Lite launches to non‑peak hours when possible.
Risk: Measurement confusion due to model performance changes. Mitigation: normalize historical throughput by workload archetype and attach a simple calibration step in the simulator.
